name: Deterministic polynomial identity testing
question: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time identity test for general arithmetic circuits?
first_attack: Specify the field/circuit/degree model; prove a deterministic hitting set for one explicit restricted class
dispatch_next: Lock paragraph is complete in research/M088_LOCK.md; implement the falsifier against that exact GF(2) degree-≤3 ≤20-gate black-box class before attaching a verifier or widening the class.
dispatch_why: The restricted class is locked in research/M088_LOCK.md. A checker without that lock does not raise readiness; the next product is a falsifier against the lock.

campaign.hypothesis: A deterministic polynomial-size hitting set can be obtained for a named restricted arithmetic circuit class.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: State field characteristic, circuit shape, degree and oracle model, then prove the exact hitting property.
campaign.next_experiment: Implement small exact circuits in the locked class and a falsifier that searches for a nonzero circuit vanishing on a proposed hitting set.
campaign.falsification: A nonzero circuit in the declared class vanishing at every proposed hitting-set point.
campaign.blocker: Restricted class locked in research/M088_LOCK.md (GF(2), degree ≤ 3, ≤ 20 gates, black-box oracle). Hitting-set lemma and independent falsifier are not yet implemented.

formal_statement.encodes: Existence of a finite hitting set for a finite circuit catalog; restricted lock documented in research/M088_LOCK.md.
not_encoded: A concrete hitting set for the locked class
